title: Common Deployment Mistakes
learning_outcomes: Explain the key behavior of common deployment mistakes and identify when it should be used.
Configure or review the workflow fields and permissions relevant to common deployment mistakes.
Verify the result using a controlled run or static check and interpret the evidence.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on common deployment mistakes. Deployment mistakes include publishing a different artifact from the one tested, running migrations without compatibility plans, and deploying without health checks or recovery. Use the example to predict the workflow result, then verify the behavior in a safe test repository or by static review.
content.why_it_matters: Common Deployment Mistakes matters because it affects correctness, security, maintainability, or operating cost. Inventory triggers, permissions, dependencies, runner assumptions, and rollback needs before changing workflows.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Deployment mistakes include publishing a different artifact from the one tested, running migrations without compatibility plans, and deploying without health checks or recovery. Migrations and maintenance should preserve observable behavior while removing legacy assumptions. Inventory triggers, permissions, dependencies, runner assumptions, and rollback needs before changing workflows. The most useful check is one that produces observable evidence and fails clearly when its stated requirement is not met.

items.title: Deploying the wrong branch or commit
items.text: Use filters to reduce unnecessary runs only when skipped work is genuinely unrelated. Include shared dependencies and test the changed and unchanged path cases so required checks are not bypassed.

items.title: Deploying without required approvals
items.text: Use a GitHub Environment for deployment-specific secrets, variables, branch restrictions, and reviewer gates. Do not treat an environment name alone as proof that approval rules are configured.

items.title: Using development credentials in production
items.text: Store credentials in the appropriate protected secret store, pass them only to the step that needs them, and never print or save them in logs, summaries, artifacts, or caches.

items.title: Missing health checks
items.text: For missing health checks, state the expected input and result, identify the relevant workflow field or operational decision, and verify it with a controlled check plus run logs. Document the failure condition rather than relying on the YAML file merely parsing.

items.title: Overlapping deployments
items.text: For overlapping deployments, state the expected input and result, identify the relevant workflow field or operational decision, and verify it with a controlled check plus run logs. Document the failure condition rather than relying on the YAML file merely parsing.

items.title: Failing to plan rollback
items.text: For failing to plan rollback, state the expected input and result, identify the relevant workflow field or operational decision, and verify it with a controlled check plus run logs. Document the failure condition rather than relying on the YAML file merely parsing.

items.title: Rebuilding rather than promoting a verified artifact
items.text: Use an artifact for a file produced by a run, choose exact upload/download paths, set retention intentionally, and verify the downloaded file is from the intended run/job.

content_blocks.code:
name: Controlled workflow review
on: workflow_dispatch
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "Review permissions, triggers, artifacts, and recovery evidence"
content_blocks.expected_output: The manually started job prints a checklist reminder; a real review must validate the actual workflow and retain reviewed evidence.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use a test repository or static validation first. Confirm the snippet matches the repository, runner, permissions, and current GitHub documentation.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Remove temporary test workflows and never carry test credentials or sample outputs into production.

content_blocks.title: Practice and verification
content_blocks.text: Inspect the example and make one focused change related to common deployment mistakes. Predict the expected result first, then use the run instructions or a static review to check it. Record the difference between your prediction and the actual result. Do not add production secrets or grant write permissions just to make a sample pass.

items.title: Syntax and scope
items.text: Check YAML indentation and confirm whether the setting belongs at workflow, job, or step level.

items.title: Permissions and trust
items.text: Start with read-only access. If the example needs more access, explain the exact operation and reduce permissions again afterwards.

items.title: Evidence
items.text: Use the run summary and first failing step. A green result is meaningful only when the intended checks actually ran.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain common deployment mistakes, read the example, and identify a way to validate it. The wider system goal remains: Recognize common failure patterns, migrate safely, and keep knowledge current as platform behavior evolves.

content.task: Apply common deployment mistakes to a small workflow change. State the expected result first, validate the configuration, then record evidence from the run or static check.
task_acceptance_criteria: Identify the relevant event, workflow field, runner behavior, or security boundary.
Explain the expected success result and at least one failure or skip condition.
Use least privilege and a disposable/test context; do not include credentials or production resources.
hints: Start with the key behavior: Deployment mistakes include publishing a different artifact from the one tested, running migrations without compatibility plans, and deploying without health checks or recovery.
Inspect the exact event filters, permissions, expressions, inputs, and job dependencies that affect this example.

content.expected_output: The expected result is the behavior described here: Deployment mistakes include publishing a different artifact from the one tested, running migrations without compatibility plans, and deploying without health checks or recovery. The real result depends on the repository, selected ref, configured permissions, and runner availability.
troubleshooting: If a workflow never starts, verify the workflow is under `.github/workflows/`, the event and filters match, and repository/organization Actions policy allows it.
If a step fails, inspect the first failed step, exit code, stderr, installed tool versions, permissions, and runner/network state before retrying.
If a job is skipped or data is missing, inspect `if`, `needs`, outputs, artifact names/paths, and cache keys; jobs do not automatically share filesystems.
common_mistakes: Assuming YAML parsing proves the workflow runs correctly or matches the intended trigger.
Granting broad token permissions, printing environment values, or exposing a secret to untrusted code.
Using a placeholder command as evidence of a real build, test, deployment, or security scan.
summary: Deployment mistakes include publishing a different artifact from the one tested, running migrations without compatibility plans, and deploying without health checks or recovery.

Migrations and maintenance should preserve observable behavior while removing legacy assumptions. Inventory triggers, permissions, dependencies, runner assumptions, and rollback needs before changing workflows.
